newsitem.title: USA: U.S. EPA aims for Jan 1 rule on food-residue law.
newsitem.headline: U.S. EPA aims for Jan 1 rule on food-residue law.

text.p: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency hopes by Jan 1 to publish a complete agenda for implementation of the new food residue law, assistant administrator Lynn Goldman said Tuesday.
Congress passed the law this summer, ending several years of acrimony over how to update the laws.
"By Jan 1, I would like to be able to publish in the Federal Register a complete agenda for the implementation of the law," Goldman told a seminar on food-safety regulations.
The agenda would include a calendar for any rule-making that would be required, she said.
Interim guidance probably will be issued, she said.

The new law sets a single standard for residues in raw and processed foods, mandates special safeguards for foods eaten by children, renews a campaign to examine the safety on pesticides on the market and expedites licensing of safer chemicals.
